shared_elements: low-relief carving on light tan stone
horizontal register or band dividing the field
row of repeated similar forms along the top
small incised sign-like or object-like motifs
justification: Both are pale stone surfaces worked in low relief with profile figures organised into stacked horizontal registers, and each includes a band of repeated linear/hatched pattern separating an upper row of similar forms from the field below, which is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they diverge sharply: A is a fine, shallowly incised, rounded-top plaque dominated by human figures, offering furniture and sign-like glyphs, while B is a massive, boldly rounded, deeply modelled architectural pillar carved almost entirely with animals, so the subject matter, scale and carving technique are quite different.
